approaches.name: Spatial vulnerability targeting and social registry subsidy migration
approaches.description: The project applies spatial tools to the Housing Vulnerability Index for block-level targeting and uses SISBEN registry eligibility to target subsidies, including migrants. Practices: Housing Vulnerability Index spatial micro-targeting of beneficiaries; Migration of housing subsidies onto SISBEN social registry targeting.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: block-level spatial targeting of subsidy beneficiaries - cue: 'spatial analytical tools' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: The HVI will further support municipalities in the process of beneficiary targeting through the application of spatial analytical tools to enable micro-targeting of vulnerable populations within each selected neighborhood at the block level.

extra_evidence.text: The migration of both the home improvement and rental subsidy programs to the SISBEN social registry system, as such, reinforces an important GoC strategic focus on efficiency of targeting social assistance.
The inclusion of SISBEN as part of the criteria for eligibility is critical to encourage a continued mainstreaming of migrants from Venezuela into the social registry and assistance system.
Housing programs use parallel systems and are transitioning to SISBEN.

category.rationale: Technological: spatial analytics index is the targeting mechanism, not a delivery or finance tool

sector.rationale: Micro-targeting vulnerable households for subsidies is a social protection targeting function.

adoption.rationale: Digital core: HVI spatial analytics | Innovative: block-level micro-targeting within neighborhoods | Category: spatial targeting tool
